breaking.headline: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
breaking.fact: The Financial Times reported Thursday that Nvidia told manufacturing partners Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, under new U.S. export-license rules aimed at stopping advanced chips being diverted to China. It is unclear whether the halt is temporary, and Nvidia fell 3.9% on Wednesday.

breaking.headline: USTR proposes new tariff rates on 14 trading partners, including China
breaking.fact: The U.S. Trade Representative has proposed new tariff rates on 14 trading partners, including China, in a statement issued in the early American session. The move follows reports the administration is poised to unveil Section 301 findings, with the EU, Japan and South Korea capped at 15% under trade deals and China, India and Vietnam facing higher rates.

breaking.headline: World shares climb as U.S. markets close for Thanksgiving
breaking.fact: Shares advanced in Europe and Asia on Thursday while U.S. markets stayed closed for the holiday: Germany's DAX jumped 1.8%, the CAC 40 in Paris climbed 1.6% and Japan's Nikkei rose 0.9%. S&P 500 futures edged up 0.3%, and oil firmed as Middle East tensions persisted. U.S. markets reopen for a short session on Friday.

breaking.headline: Houston's 77th H-E-B Thanksgiving Day Parade steps off at 9 AM with Lizzo leading
breaking.fact: The 77th Annual H-E-B Thanksgiving Day Parade rolls through downtown Houston this morning at 9 AM, with hometown star Lizzo as grand marshal. The parade features 15 floats and 10 giant balloons, including a 50-foot Popeye, along a route from Smith and Lamar. Watching from public areas along the route is free.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide is trading in Paris this morning at €189.92, worth $207.68 at the ECB's Nov 25 reference rate of 1.0935, up about 0.8% in dollars while U.S. markets sit out Thanksgiving. The industrial-gas giant keeps grinding steadily higher as American tech gives back its rally, its defensive profile doing quiet work. With no company news, the dollar price mostly tracks the euro near the top of its range.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic closed Wednesday at $82.79, up 1.1% as the stock steadied after sliding below its $83 IPO price on Tuesday. The AI name got caught in the chip selloff earlier in the week, but Wednesday's bounce put it back near breakeven on the debut. Sean's IPO allocation is a long-term hold, not a trade. Watch whether it can hold above the IPO price once Friday's short session resumes.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL edged up a penny Wednesday to $91.64, the quiet government-cash anchor doing its job while growth stocks slid into the holiday. Its $0.30849 distribution, ex Nov 2 and paid Nov 5, carries a 4.04% distribution yield. With a December Fed hike now seen as nearly certain, short Treasury yields stay supported. Markets are closed for Thanksgiving, so BIL simply holds its value until Friday's short session.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet fell 2.1% Wednesday to $273.10, giving back more of the week's gains as the Nasdaq slid 0.6% and chips led the decline. The AI spending question cuts both ways for Google: its cloud business benefits, but the capital outlays keep growing. With U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving, the next test comes Friday. The AI and search thesis is intact, but the tape stays rough into the weekend.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly slipped 1.1% Wednesday to $1,392.22, a modest pullback after Tuesday's 3.2% jump as money rotated to defensive growth. Moody's lifted Lilly to Aa2 this week, citing the weight-loss drug franchise's growth. With the Fed leaning hawkish, Lilly's drug-driven earnings look comparatively safe. The stock remains near the top of its range, and the GLP-1 story still has room to run into the new year.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere Energy jumped 2.0% Wednesday to $301.99, showing steady strength while oil whipsawed and the market fell. Natural-gas export demand stays firm, and the Strait of Hormuz tensions keep energy in focus, though Cheniere's U.S. Gulf Coast terminals sit far from the strait. The stock has been a quiet outperformer this fall. Watch the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday and winter gas demand for the next move.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia fell 3.9% Wednesday to $149.30, giving back more of Monday's 31% surge after Huang's reinstatement, and the pressure continued overnight: the FT reports Nvidia told Dell and Supermicro to halt AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries under new U.S. export-license rules. Sean's call stands: a long-term hold until the probes and investigation shake out, with Huang testifying Dec 1.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer was flat Wednesday at $28.46, holding Tuesday's 3.9% gain as investors rotated into defensive dividend payers. The drugmaker's yield and steady cash flow look attractive with the Fed leaning toward another hike and growth stocks under pressure. Pfizer remains well off its highs, and the dividend is the core of the thesis here. Watch for any pipeline or deal news to give the stock a second leg.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab jumped 2.3% Wednesday to $47.02, bouncing with the market's late-day recovery after Tuesday's 7.4% slide. The space stock has been volatile all month, swinging with risk appetite rather than company news. No fresh launch or contract headlines drove the move; it was the tape. The long-term launch-cadence story is unchanged, but the stock needs calmer markets to find a footing.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital rose 2.9% Wednesday to $8.92, extending a strong week as the mortgage REIT's dividend yield drew buyers. Higher-for-longer rates are a mixed blessing for Rithm: they pressure book value but fatten the spreads on new investments. The stock has been climbing steadily this month. Watch the December Fed decision and the direction of mortgage rates for the next leg.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SPCX, the leveraged S&P 500 fund, rose 1.3% Wednesday to $127.44, tracking the market's late recovery with its usual amplified move as the S&P 500 cut its losses. Leveraged funds magnify both directions, and this week was all downside until Wednesday's rebound. It is a trading vehicle, not a buy-and-hold, and sharp down days are the cost of leverage. Watch Friday's short session for the next swing.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist Financial rose 0.9% Wednesday to $47.89, holding up as the Dow climbed above 50,000 for the first time and banks caught a bid. Regional banks benefit from the steepening rate outlook as the Fed leans hawkish, and Truist's dividend adds ballast. The stock has been grinding higher this month while tech whipsaws. Watch the December Fed meeting and the rate path driving bank earnings.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony rose 1.4% Wednesday to $2.21, steadying after Tuesday's 8.8% slide as small miners sold off. China's antimony and chip-material export curbs stay on hold until January, so no new policy pressure, but the stock trades on sentiment. The long-term domestic-supply thesis is intact, and the company remains a speculative bet. Watch for defense or critical-minerals news to spark the next move.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy rose 2.2% Wednesday to $5.69, recovering part of Tuesday's 4.6% slide in the market's late rebound. The uranium story still rests on nuclear expansion and government buying, but the stock is hostage to risk appetite in the meantime. UEC remains a favorite long-term holding, and Sean wants to add while the price is low. Watch for reactor or contracting headlines and a turn in sentiment.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: VI5TC is estimated at $147.64, down 0.3% on the S&P 500's Wednesday slide, using the S&P-anchored estimator recalibrated from Sean's account value. The fund tracks the broad market, so its move simply mirrors the index, which fell as tech gave back gains before recovering. The estimate updates with each S&P close and stays marked as an estimate. Watch Friday's short session for the market's next direction.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero Energy slipped 0.5% Wednesday to $323.00 even as the Dow hit 50,000, as oil seesawed and refiners gave back gains. Brent held near $91 with the Hormuz tensions competing against surplus worries ahead of the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday. Valero's refining margins remain the swing factor, and the dividend keeps paying while the stock consolidates. Watch OPEC+ and winter fuel demand for direction.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: The Target Retirement 2035 fund's NAV edged up to $28.45 as of Nov 25, a small gain as stocks recovered from intraday lows and bonds held steady. The diversified target-date fund does the quiet work of the portfolio, blending U.S. and international stocks with bonds that glide more conservative with time. Wednesday's move was modest beside the Nasdaq's swings. It remains a set-and-forget core holding for 2035.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: SWVXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Schwab's 7-day SEC yield at 3.79% as published Nov 25, up a touch from 3.78%. The sweep fund keeps shrinking by design: whenever it tops $1,000 in an account, cash moves into a CD, and the position should evaporate over time. It trails Vanguard's Treasury fund, but stays the Schwab sweep vehicle. Leftover pennies sweep to the mutual-fund remnants as an account nears zero.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: VUSXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Vanguard's 7-day SEC yield at 4.01% as published Nov 25, down a touch from 4.04%. The Treasury money-market fund is the eTrade cash home and the landing spot for the Seiver Slough and Seiver Lodge sale proceeds down the road. It pays more than Schwab's SWVXX and carries no ticket fee at eTrade. The yield should stay supported with a December Fed hike now nearly certain.

weekInBrief.headline: Bank of Korea resumes rate hikes, lifting its benchmark to 3.25%
weekInBrief.body: The Bank of Korea raised its base rate by a quarter point to 3.25% on Thursday, resuming its tightening cycle after an October pause, as a chip-driven export boom keeps inflation and housing prices elevated. The 5-2 decision also lifted the bank's growth forecast to 3.9% for 2026 and 4.1% for 2027.

weekInBrief.headline: Bank of England warns more hikes likely if energy prices stay high
weekInBrief.body: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey told Parliament on Wednesday that it is more likely than not the bank will have to raise interest rates further if energy prices stay elevated, as the bank publishes its Financial Stability Report today. The warning comes as the Middle East conflict keeps oil near $91 a barrel.

weekInBrief.headline: Bank of Japan's Tamura says a 50-point hike may be needed
weekInBrief.body: Bank of Japan board member Naoki Tamura said on Thursday that the central bank must keep raising interest rates regardless of upside and downside price risks, as long as underlying inflation stays around 2%, and that a 50-basis-point hike may be needed if inflation risks materialize. The yen held near 159.20 to the dollar.

weekInBrief.headline: U.S. crude stocks rose 1.1 million barrels last week, EIA says
weekInBrief.body: U.S. crude inventories rose 1.1 million barrels to 418.9 million in the week ended November 20, the Energy Information Administration said, less than the 1.5 million-barrel build analysts expected. The modest build supported prices alongside the Middle East supply worries, with WTI holding near $85.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Two more tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting sea mines north of Oman's Khasab port on Thursday, the Revolutionary Guards said, claiming the vessels were on an unauthorized route — one was a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude; the claims remain unverified and the vessels unnamed. Britain's maritime trade agency separately reported an explosion from an unknown projectile near a tanker about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai on Thursday. Yemen's Houthis said they had struck Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery and Saudi ports, pushing oil higher on supply concerns, though Gulf oil supply had been recovering toward pre-war levels before the latest disruptions. Kpler's latest data still puts Iranian crude loadings at zero, with Iranian oil on the water down below 50 million barrels and only about 4.5 million barrels left outside the blockade zone to discharge, while total Gulf crude exports — counting the Saudi and UAE bypass pipelines — are running at about 16.7 million barrels a day, just shy of the roughly 17 million before the war.

space.headline: A giant lambda-shaped stellar nursery hides in the Milky Way's outskirts
space.body: Astronomers have found a giant hub-filament system of molecular gas in the outer Milky Way, dubbed the lambda-complex, about 43,000 light-years from the galactic center and 16,800 light-years from the Sun. The structure, G195.65-0.10, holds 61 dense gas clumps where stars are forming, and it behaves much like the star-forming regions closer to the galaxy's center despite the harsher environment.

space.headline: Gut microbes adapt as we age, a 10,000-person study finds
space.body: A study of more than 10,000 people, published in Nature, found specific mutations in gut bacteria that arise during human ageing — but few linked to disease. The authors singled out one adaptation that helps one of the most abundant gut species resist oxidative stress, the cell damage that increases with age. The gut's bacterial community itself usually stays stable over a lifetime.

space.headline: New maps of a heart receptor point to better drugs for heart failure
space.body: A Harvard team has revealed that the two types of drugs now being tested for heart failure and pulmonary fibrosis activate the RXFP1 relaxin receptor in different ways: the protein relaxin-2 binds a part sticking out of the cell surface, while the small molecule AZD5462 binds directly inside the membrane. The work, published in Science, opens at least two distinct sites on the receptor for drug design.

space.headline: A molecular backdoor destroys the 'undruggable' protein behind Ewing sarcoma
space.body: Penn State researchers found a way to destroy the rogue fusion protein that drives Ewing sarcoma, a rare bone and soft-tissue cancer in children, by blocking CK2, the enzyme that stabilizes it. In preclinical studies the drug silmitasertib broke down the fusion protein, slowed tumor spread and prolonged survival in mice — and a Phase I clinical trial is already underway.

apod.title: Eye in the Sky: The Milky Way over Lençóis
apod.explanation: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder. The Milky Way shines bright in the sky of Brazil, over the white sand dunes and dark lagoons of Lençóis Maranhenses National Park. This composite image was taken later in the night in July from a latitude of approximately 2º south, and shows prominent Milky Way features such as dark dust lanes and colorful nebulas. The arched, rainbow-like shape is an artifact of the wide-angle lens — as the Galaxy was artfully framed, it matches the contour of the dark lagoon, creating the illusion of a cosmic eye, half in space and half on the ground.
